entities.name: Quintus Pompeius Sosius Falco
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Pompeius Sosius Falco was a Roman senator during the reign of Commodus, serving as consul ordinarius in 193 alongside Gaius Julius Erucius Clarus Vibianus. He played a significant role in the governance of the Roman Empire, contributing to the political landscape of the time.





 Falco's influence extended beyond his tenure as consul, as he was part of a broader network of Roman senators who shaped the empire's policies and decisions. His involvement in the governance of the Roman Empire had a lasting impact on the development of the empire's political system.





 Despite the significance of his role, very little is known about Falco's personal life, making him one of the lesser-known figures in Roman history. However, his contributions to the Roman Empire's governance are undeniable, and his legacy continues to be studied by historians today.
